agent: wave 12 agent C - the effect side of the event script language
question: CEffect's virtual table slot map; the behaviour of the busiest effects; CContextEffect as the effect-side twin of CContextTrigger; and what Execute's second stack argument is
slots_noted: CEffect slot 10's base body (rva 0x59CB20) is left unnamed as a function. It is a folded 'set the out string to empty and return it' body, held 99 times - 98 at slot 10 of a CEffect-family table and once at slot 2 of CStatisticsLedger, which is not in the family - so naming it for CEffect would be trap 4. The slot itself is recorded under CEffect as GetTargetText, from what the three overriders produce and from how slot 8 uses the result. CEffect slots 1, 2, 3 and 5 are deliberately not recorded here: they hold CPersistent's own bodies (Save 0x5BB10, the folded empty SaveContents 0x20CD50, Load 0x67C050 and the folded empty AfterLoad 0x6BF890) and project.json already records those slots on CPersistent, which covers every table below it. Slot 7's body is already recorded as CEffect::TakeScalarValue; the slot name is added here. CEffect +0x14 is left unnamed: nothing in the three destructors or in CEffect::LoadKey touches it.

addresses.name: CEffect::Execute
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CEffect::Execute(CEffect* this, CEventScope* scope, int unused)
addresses.comment: **Slot 11, and the base's own body: run every child effect against the same scope.** 0x59C6E0 to the single `ret 8` at 0x59C709, 0x2C bytes, followed by four int3. It walks the child list at `this+8` - payload at node+0, next at node+8, the same CList shape CTrigger uses - and dispatches `[vftable+0x2C]`, slot 11, on each child with **both** arguments pushed through unchanged. That is the self-referential proof that slot 11 is the recursive execute, the same argument FINDINGS-script.md used for CTrigger slot 6; ten `*Effect::Execute` bodies project.json already names sit at slot 11 of their own tables, and all 100 distinct slot-11 bodies in the family end `ret 8`. Held by CEffect and CMultipleTargetEffect, which does not override it. **The second argument is read by nothing**: of the 100 slot-11 bodies, 11 read `[ebp+0xC]` and every one of the 11 only pushes it into its own child dispatch, while CRandomEffect and CContextEffect substitute a literal 0 - so it carries no information any effect uses.
addresses.evidence: The body decoded end to end; `ret 8` on the one exit with four int3 after it. Slot membership read as vftable+11*4 out of the RTTI tables for all 101 CEffect-family classes that have one. The arguments: `mov ebx,[ebp+8]` / `mov edi,[ebp+0xC]` then `push edi; push ebx` before `call edx`, so the order is preserved. The 'nothing reads it' claim is a scan of all 100 slot-11 bodies for a read of [ebp+0xC], bounded by the next known function entry, with the positive control that the same scan sees [ebp+8] in 98 of the 100. Shown wrong by: any slot-11 body that reads [ebp+0xC] and does something with it other than pass it on, or a caller that depends on the value.

addresses.name: CEffect::GetBlockText
addresses.signature: Hoi3CString* __thiscall CEffect::GetBlockText(CEffect* this, Hoi3CString* out, CEventScope* scope, int depth, Hoi3CString group, int unknown)
addresses.comment: **Slot 8: the whole of an effect block as the tooltip shows it, indented.** 0x59C710 to the single `ret 0x2C` at 0x59CB0E. It appends three spaces (the literal at 0x11F39A8) `depth` times, asks its own slot 9 (`[vftable+0x24]`) for its sentence, then walks the children at `this+8`. For each child it calls the child's **slot 10** for a short label and compares `child->slot6()` with the next child's; while they are equal and the label is non-empty it appends `\xA7W,\xA7Y ` (0x11F39AC, six characters) and keeps collecting, and when the run ends it calls the child's **slot 8** with the collected text as the `group` argument and the same depth and trailing int. So consecutive effects built by the same keyword are rendered as one comma-separated line, and slot 6 - the keyword token - is the grouping key. The recursion into slot 8 with an identical argument shape is what fixes the signature. 87 of the 101 family tables hold this body; the 14 that override it are the scope and iteration effects (`any_*`, `random_*`, `region`, `CContextEffect`), which is the same split as CContextTrigger's on the trigger side.
addresses.evidence: Decoded end to end, 0x401 bytes, one `ret 0x2C`, which the signature's 4+4+4+0x1C+4 predicts exactly (Hoi3CString by value is 0x1C, per checkSignatures.py's own table). The slot numbers are read off the dispatch displacements: 0x24 is slot 9, 0x28 slot 10, 0x20 slot 8, 0x18 slot 6. Shown wrong by: a different reading of the displacement arithmetic, or an argument order that does not match the recursive call site at 0x59C98B-0x59C9C3.

addresses.name: CEffect::GetText
addresses.signature: Hoi3CString* __thiscall CEffect::GetText(CEffect* this, Hoi3CString* out, CEventScope* scope, Hoi3CString group, int unknown)
addresses.comment: **Slot 9: one effect as one sentence, and the base says nothing.** 0x5B0ED0 to the `ret 0x28` at 0x5B0F30, 0x63 bytes. It sets `*out` to the shared empty string (0x11B4945), destroys the by-value `group` string it was handed and returns `out`. 24 of the 101 family tables keep it, so 77 effects write their own sentence; the four `*Effect::GetText` bodies project.json already names - CKillLeaderEffect 0x5ADD30, CAddDivisionEffect 0x5B5FA0, CLoadOOBEffect 0x5BBE40, CPracticalEffect 0x5BDDB0 - all sit at slot 9. The third parameter is the text slot 8 collected from the grouped siblings' slot 10, which is what those four signatures call `unread`: the base does read it, if only to free it.
addresses.evidence: Decoded end to end; `ret 0x28` matches 4+4+0x1C+4. The `group` parameter's position is fixed by slot 8's call site at 0x59C7AD-0x59C7DB, which reserves 0x1C bytes with `sub esp,0x1c` and copies [ebp+0x14] into it with std::string::assignString before pushing out and scope. Shown wrong by: the four recorded leaf GetText bodies not all sitting at slot 9, or a different size for Hoi3CString by value.

addresses.name: CEffect::GetKeywordToken
addresses.signature: SaveToken __thiscall CEffect::GetKeywordToken(CEffect* this)
addresses.comment: **Slot 6, and the whole body is `mov eax,[ecx+0x18]; ret`.** The field it returns is written in exactly one place in the image: the common tail of `CEffect::LoadKey` at 0x59B630, `if (newEffect) newEffect->+0x18 = key`, where `key` is LoadKey's own third argument - the SaveToken of the keyword that built the effect. So +0x18 is 'which keyword made me', and slot 6 is its getter. Every one of the 101 CEffect-family classes with a table holds this body at slot 6 and **none overrides it**, which is inheritance rather than folding (trap 4) - the holders are one family and nothing outside it holds the body at all. Its one reader is `CEffect::GetBlockText`, which uses it to decide whether two adjacent children belong on the same tooltip line. FINDINGS-script.md already noted this body as 'slot 6 means something else on CEffect ... a plain getter'; this says what of.
addresses.evidence: Three instructions, read as bytes: 8b 41 18 c3, then twelve int3. A decode of all 8136 bytes of CEffect::LoadKey finds exactly one write to a `+0x18` that is not esp-relative, at 0x59B630, and cfg.py --lands-in shows 0x59B625 is the convergence point every arm of the switch jumps to. vtable.py --holding gives 101 holders, all at slot 6, all in the CEffect family. Shown wrong by: another writer of +0x18 reached from somewhere this decode did not cover, or a holder of 0x16000 outside the family.

addresses.name: CEffect::~CEffect
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CEffect::~CEffect(CEffect* this, char freeMemory)
addresses.comment: **Slot 0, the virtual deleting destructor.** 0x59C540 to the `ret 4` at 0x59C5BB. It writes CEffect's own vftable (0x11B58F4) into the object, frees every node of the child list at `this+8` through the list helper at 0x4B6260 and the plain `free`, zeroes +8/+0xC/+0x10, then frees `this` when the flag argument has bit 0 set, and returns `this` in EAX. 74 of the 101 family tables hold it; nine other bodies appear at slot 0, of which 0x59C4E0 is the one the eleven string-valued effects share (it frees the Hoi3CString at +0x20 first, through 0x59C5C0). **It does not touch +0x20**, which is the clearest single piece of evidence that CEffect itself has no string there and that a derived effect's own data starts at 0x20.
addresses.evidence: Decoded end to end; the `test byte ptr [ebp+8], 1` / `call free` / `mov eax, ebx` shape is MSVC's deleting destructor and the `ret 4` agrees. 74 holders at slot 0, all in the family, so related() is satisfied and the class name is not a fold. Shown wrong by: a reference to this body from outside the CEffect family, or a slot-0 holder that is not a CEffect.

addresses.name: CContextEffect::Execute
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CContextEffect::Execute(CContextEffect* this, CEventScope* scope, int unused)
addresses.comment: **Slot 11, and the effect side of scoping narrows exactly as the trigger side does.** 0x59E2B0 to the one `ret 8` at 0x59E2FB, 0x4C bytes, two int3 then CContextEffect::GetText at 0x59E300. It builds a 0x48-byte CEventScope on its own stack, calls `CEventScope::MakeScope(scope, this->spec (+0x20), &out)` - the same already-recorded function (0x5C1C10) CContextTrigger uses, which copy-constructs the receiver into `out` and then overwrites only country and/or province - tests `out.resolved (+0x3C)`, and only then walks its children dispatching slot 11 on each with `&out`. So `GER = { ... }` or `owner = { ... }` in an effect block **narrows the scope it was given rather than building a new one**, and the ten context tokens and their meanings are the ones FINDINGS-triggereval.md read. Two differences from the trigger side worth having: an unresolvable context here is a **silent no-op** rather than a false, so the rest of the block still runs; and the children are passed a literal **0** as the second argument, not this effect's own. 10,686 live instances.
addresses.evidence: Decoded end to end. The `cmp byte ptr [esp+0x44], 0` at 0x59E2CD resolves to out+0x3C once the two intervening pushes are accounted for, and FINDINGS-triggereval.md independently lists 0x59E2CD as one of the two effect-side readers of CEventScope::resolved - two readings agreeing without either being derived from the other. `push 0` at 0x59E2EA is the second argument of the child dispatch. Shown wrong by: the stack arithmetic landing on a different field of `out`, or MakeScope being reached with something other than this+0x20.

addresses.name: CContextEffect::GetBlockText
addresses.signature: Hoi3CString* __thiscall CContextEffect::GetBlockText(CContextEffect* this, Hoi3CString* out, CEventScope* scope, int depth, Hoi3CString group, int unknown)
addresses.comment: **Slot 8, the third and last caller of CEventScope::MakeScope on the effect side - and the one that does not test `resolved`.** 0x59E520 to the one `ret 0x2C` at 0x59E93F. It indents by depth, asks its own slot 9 for the context's own line, then calls MakeScope at 0x59E635 and walks its children against the **new** scope, grouping them by slot 6 exactly as the base does. It never reads `out.resolved (+0x3C)`, whereas slots 11 and 9 both do - so a context that resolves to nothing still has its children described in the tooltip against a scope the executor refuses. That is the same asymmetry FINDINGS-triggereval.md found between CContextTrigger::Evaluate and its CountEvaluation/GetBlockText, arrived at from the other half of the language.
addresses.evidence: Decoded end to end, 0x422 bytes, one `ret 0x2C` which 4+4+4+0x1C+4 predicts. The MakeScope call at 0x59E635 is a direct call to the recorded 0x5C1C10 with `lea eax,[edi+0x20]` as the spec. The absence of a +0x3C read is a scan of the whole decoded body for `0x8c`/`0x3c` displacements off the scope locals, with the positive control that the same scan finds the read in slot 11 and in slot 9. Shown wrong by: a read of out+0x3C anywhere in the body.

addresses.name: CSetCountryFlagEffect::Execute
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CSetCountryFlagEffect::Execute(CSetCountryFlagEffect* this, CEventScope* scope, int unused)
addresses.comment: **`set_country_flag`, 8,120 live instances.** 0x5A4970 to two `ret 8` exits at 0x5A49C3 and 0x5A49D1, twelve int3 after. It takes the flag name out of its own Hoi3CString at `this+0x20` (SSO test on +0x34), finds the country as `CCountryDataBase ([0x1A855A4]) ->+0x16C[scope->country_id (+0x14)]`, and calls **slot 2 of the CFlags held by value at `CCountry +0x180`** with the name. That slot is the already-recorded `GuiTypeTree_Find` (rva 0x67DEE0), which walks the ternary search tree at `TernarySearchTreeFind` (0x67E030) - so **a country flag lookup is case-insensitive**, because that walk calls tolower on each query byte and `TernarySearchTreeInsert` lowercases each byte it stores. On a hit it writes `CFlag::is_set (+0x1C) = 1`, the byte CFlags.hpp already names from the reader side. On a miss it calls 0x4D640, which creates the flag. So setting a flag always succeeds.
addresses.evidence: Decoded end to end. `CCountry +0x180 flags CFlags` and `CFlag +0x1C is_set` were already in project.json and in BiceLib/GameClasses/CFlags.hpp, named from CFlags::IsFlagSet - so the writer found here agrees with the reader already recorded, which is the control. The case-insensitivity is inherited from project.json's own description of 0x67E030 and 0x4DA70, not read again here. Shown wrong by: CFlags' slot 2 being something other than 0x67DEE0, or `[eax+0x1c]` being a different field of whatever slot 2 returns.

addresses.name: CClrCountryFlagEffect::Execute
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CClrCountryFlagEffect::Execute(CClrCountryFlagEffect* this, CEventScope* scope, int unused)
addresses.comment: **`clr_country_flag`, 9,057 live instances - the busiest leaf effect in the family - and it is not the mirror of `set_country_flag`.** 0x5A49E0 to the one `ret 8` at 0x5A4A2C, one int3 then the next function at 0x5A4A30 (trap 2: a single 0xCC of padding). Same lookup as the setter, and on a hit it writes `CFlag::is_set (+0x1C) = 0`. **On a miss it does nothing** - there is no call to the creator at 0x4D640 anywhere in the body. So clearing a flag that was never set leaves no record of the clear, which matters only in that `has_country_flag` on a never-set flag and on a cleared one are indistinguishable; the two paths differ in cost, not in result.
addresses.evidence: Decoded end to end, 0x4D bytes, with the whole miss path being `je` past the single store. The setter at 0x5A4970 has the extra arm and this one does not, read side by side. Shown wrong by: a second exit from this body that this decode missed - but the one `ret 8` is the only exit cfg.walk finds.

addresses.name: CFlags_AddFlag
addresses.signature: CFlag* __stdcall CFlags_AddFlag(CFlags* flags@stack:4, const char* name@EDI) @EAX
addresses.comment: **Create a flag and put it in the tree.** 0x4D640 to the `ret 4` at 0x4D692, eleven int3 after. `operator new(0x20)` - so **a CFlag is 0x20 bytes**, the 0x1C-byte Hoi3CString at +0 plus the `is_set` byte at +0x1C and padding - then `is_set = 1`, `name.assign(name, strlen(name))`, and slot 6 of the container with the new element passed twice: that slot is the already-recorded `NameTree_Insert` (rva 0x4D8A0), whose name argument is a `std::string*` and whose value is the element, which works because CFlag's name is at offset 0. Returns the new element. **The name is in EDI, not on the stack** - the compiler left it in a register variable - so this is not a __thiscall and carries no `::` (trap 11). Recorded class-free because it is in no vftable and the container is only ever reached as a `CFlags`-shaped object; the three `set_*_flag` effects are its callers along with 0x4D6A0 nearby.
addresses.evidence: Decoded end to end; `push 0x20; call operator_new` then the three stores, and `ret 4` with one stack argument. EDI is never written in the body before `mov eax, edi` at 0x4D667, and all three callers hold the name in EDI at the call. project.json already records 0x4D8A0 as slot 6 of this family of name trees. addresses.name: CIntEffect::TakeScalarValue
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CIntEffect::TakeScalarValue(CIntEffect* this, CToken value)
addresses.comment: **Slot 7 for the twenty-one integer-valued effect keywords, and the place the thousandths convention enters the script language.** 0x59D4A0 to three `ret 0x104` exits at 0x59D4BF/0x59D4CF/0x59D4E9, four int3 after. It clears `use_this`/`use_from` (+0x1C/+0x1D) and the value at +0x20, then: token 0x377 (`this`) sets +0x1C, token 0x34F (`from`) sets +0x1D, and anything else is `atoi(text) * 1000` into +0x20 (`imul eax, eax, 0x3e8`). **So an integer effect's number is stored in thousandths and anything after the decimal point is lost before the multiply** - `national_unity = 2.5` is 2, not 2.5. The control is `CCountryEventEffect::Execute`, which divides +0x20 by 1000 to get the event id back, and `CRandomEffect::Execute`, which divides it by 1000 to get a percentage. Held at slot 7 by 21 classes, all deriving from CIntEffect, so it is inheritance and not a fold.
addresses.evidence: Decoded end to end. `atoi` is 0xB969F1 reached with `lea eax,[ebp+0xc]`, the text of the CToken, and `imul eax, eax, 0x3e8` is the only arithmetic in the body. Two independent consumers divide by 1000 (0x5AE4BA and 0x5AF962, both the 0x10624dd3/sar 6 idiom). vtable.py --holding: 21 holders, all slot 7, all CIntEffect descendants. Shown wrong by: a consumer of +0x20 on an integer effect that does not divide by 1000.

addresses.name: CValueEffect::TakeScalarValue
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CValueEffect::TakeScalarValue(CValueEffect* this, CToken value)
addresses.comment: **Slot 7 for the eleven fixed-point effect keywords** - `dissent`, `neutrality`, `manpower`, `leadership`, `organisation`, `popularity`, `revoltrisk`, `warexhaustion`, `officer_pool`, `change_manpower`, `split_troops`. 0x59CB50 to three `ret 0x104` exits, the last at 0x59CB8C. Same `this`/`from` handling as the integer form, but the number goes through `ParseThousandths` (rva 0x6696A0) instead of atoi, so **these keywords do accept up to three decimal places**: `dissent = 2.5` is 2500 and means 2.5. That is the one real difference between the two scalar families and it is invisible in the script. Held at slot 7 by 11 classes, all CValueEffect descendants.
addresses.evidence: Decoded end to end; the only call in the body is to 0x6696A0 with (&token, &this->+0x20). The eleven holders are read off the RTTI tables. Shown wrong by: 0x6696A0 not being a thousandths parser, which its own body settles.

addresses.name: ParseThousandths
addresses.signature: bool __stdcall ParseThousandths(CToken* value, int* out)
addresses.comment: **Where 'numbers are thousandths' is implemented for the script language.** 0x6696A0 to the last of three `ret 8` exits at 0x6697A3 (the others are 0x6696D3, the no-fraction answer, and 0x669701). `sscanf(text, "%i", &whole)`; a false return when that finds nothing. With no `.` in the text (strchr against 0x11B5C64) the answer is `whole * 1000`. With one, it copies **up to three** characters after the dot into a `"000"` template - the literal 0x303030, written into the first argument's own stack slot, which the function has finished with - skips leading zeros, `sscanf`es that, negates it when the whole part was negative, and answers `whole * 1000 + fraction`. So a fourth decimal place is silently dropped and `0.5` is 500. The text is read from `value + 4`, so the argument is the `{ SaveToken token; char text[0x100] }` pair project.json spells `CToken`. Ten callers across the image, so this is the general reader and not something the effects own.
addresses.evidence: Decoded end to end. `imul ecx, ecx, 0x3e8` on both paths, the three-character cap is `cmp ecx, 3; jge`, and the "000" template is the immediate 0x303030. findRefs.py --callers gives 10 direct calls. Shown wrong by: the format string at 0x11FD14C not being "%i" - the bytes there are `%i\0`, read directly.

addresses.name: CCountry::ChangeNationalUnity
addresses.signature: void __fastcall CCountry::ChangeNationalUnity(CCountry* this@ESI, int delta@stack:4)
addresses.comment: **The only writer of `CCountry +0x10B8`, national unity.** 0x4F8B80 minus the base: 0xF8B80 to the `ret 4` at 0xF8BD5, eight int3 after. `scale = global_modifier.values (+0xDA8) [MODIFIER_NATIONAL_UNITY_EFFECT] + 1000`, then `this->+0x10B8 += delta * scale / 1000` through the 64-bit divide helper 0xB99980, clamped to at most 100000 and at least 1000 - i.e. **national unity lives in thousandths and is held between 1.0 and 100.0**. The country arrives in ESI and the delta on the stack, the same convention as `CCountry::ChangeNeutrality` (0xFBF80) beside it. Its one caller found here is `CNationalUnityEffect::Execute`.
addresses.evidence: Decoded end to end. The modifier index is the displacement 0x220 off the values pointer; a modifier entry is 8 bytes (trap 5), so 0x220/8 = 68 = 0x44, and scripts/modifierIds.py gives id 0x44 as MODIFIER_NATIONAL_UNITY_EFFECT - the modifier's own name confirms the function's. `CCountry +0xD90` is already recorded as global_modifier and `CModifier::values` as +0x18, which is how +0xDA8 resolves. Shown wrong by: a second writer of +0x10B8 on a CCountry, or the entry stride being 4 rather than 8.

addresses.name: CNationalUnityEffect::Execute
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CNationalUnityEffect::Execute(CNationalUnityEffect* this, CEventScope* scope, int unused)
addresses.comment: **`national_unity`.** 0x5B19D0 to the one `ret 8` at 0x5B1A0D. `if (this->+0x20 != 0) CCountry::ChangeNationalUnity(db->+0x16C[scope->country_id], this->+0x20)`. addresses.name: CNeutralityEffect::Execute
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CNeutralityEffect::Execute(CNeutralityEffect* this, CEventScope* scope, int unused)
addresses.comment: **`neutrality`.** 0x5B9740 to the one `ret 8` at 0x5B977D. `if (this->+0x20 != 0) CCountry::ChangeNeutrality(db->+0x16C[scope->country_id], this->+0x20, true)` - the already-recorded setter, writing `CCountry +0xA8C`. The `true` is the `logHistory` argument, so **a `neutrality` effect writes an entry into the country's history list, which the daily drift does not**. The value comes through `CValueEffect::TakeScalarValue`, so it is fixed point: `neutrality = -2.5` is -2500 and means -2.5.
addresses.evidence: Decoded end to end, one `ret 8`, `push 1` as the third argument of 0xFBF80 whose recorded signature names it logHistory and whose comment says the daily pass passes false. Shown wrong by: the push order being the other way round, which the recorded `ret 8` on ChangeNeutrality plus the stack temp for the delta pins down.

addresses.name: CDissentEffect::Execute
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CDissentEffect::Execute(CDissentEffect* this, CEventScope* scope, int unused)
addresses.comment: **`dissent`, and the independent confirmation that `CCountry +0x10B4` is dissent.** 0x5BA0B0 to the one `ret 8` at 0x5BA108. `if (this->+0x20 != 0) { country->+0x10B4 += this->+0x20; if (that went negative) country->+0x10B4 = 0; }` - written inline, with no setter and **no upper clamp**. The value is fixed point through `CValueEffect::TakeScalarValue`. project.json already named +0x10B4 `dissent` from the daily pass zeroing it for the rebel country; this is a second, unrelated writer agreeing.
addresses.evidence: Decoded end to end, one `ret 8`, the two stores both to +0x10B4 of the object the country database yields for scope->country_id. The agreement with the recorded field name is the control. Shown wrong by: +0x10B4 not being dissent, which would also break the existing record.

addresses.name: CAddCountryModifierEffect::Execute
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CAddCountryModifierEffect::Execute(CAddCountryModifierEffect* this, CEventScope* scope, int unused)
addresses.comment: **`add_country_modifier`, 4,420 live instances, and it is idempotent in a way the scripts cannot see.** 0x5A38A0 to the one `ret 8` at 0x5A3935, eight int3 after. `this+0x24` is the CStaticModifier the loader resolved from the `name` key and `this+0x20` the `duration` key - **plain `atoi`, no thousandths, so duration is in days** (0x5A2E24 in CAddCountryModifierEffect::LoadKey). Then: **if +0x24 is null it does nothing**, which is what a misspelt modifier name produces and the load reports nothing either; it walks the country's `active_modifiers (CCountry +0x648)` and **returns without doing anything if a node's payload already points at the same CStaticModifier**, so re-applying a modifier a country already has neither stacks it nor refreshes its duration; otherwise it calls 0x5DFB90 - rva 0xDFB90 - with the country, the modifier's name (a Hoi3CString by value, taken from `CStaticModifier +0x2C`) and the duration.
addresses.evidence: Both bodies decoded end to end. The dedup is `mov edx,[eax]; cmp [edx+8], esi; je <exit>` inside the list walk, with esi the resolved modifier. The duration's scale is `call atoi (0xB969F1); mov [esi+0x20], eax` with no imul, read against CIntEffect::TakeScalarValue which does have one. `CCountry +0x648 active_modifiers` was already recorded. Shown wrong by: the payload's +8 not being the CStaticModifier the loader stored, or a second path into 0xDFB90 from this body.

addresses.name: CRemoveBrigadeEffect::Execute
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CRemoveBrigadeEffect::Execute(CRemoveBrigadeEffect* this, CEventScope* scope, int unused)
addresses.comment: **`remove_brigade`, 6,881 live instances, and what it matches on is not the brigade type.** 0x5BBF10 to the last of three `ret 8` exits, at rvas 0x5BC030, 0x5BC133 and 0x5BC1DB; CRemoveBrigadeEffect::GetText begins at 0x5BC1E0, which is what says the third `ret` really is the end (trap 3's vftable check). It walks the scope country's `units (CCountry +0xBAC)` and, inside each, the unit's `regiments (CUnit +0x38)`, asking each regiment for **slot 8** - a folded body (rva 0x6C6C50, five holders including CEU3DialogGuiType, so it stays unnamed) that returns a copy of `CSubUnit +0x68`, which project.json already names **`name`, the historical regiment name** - and comparing it for exact equality with the effect's own `CStringEffect::text (+0x20)`. The comparison is a plain memcmp plus a length test, so it is **case-sensitive**, unlike the flag trees. On the first match it stops: if the unit holds more than one regiment (`regiments_count +0x40 != 1`) it calls the already-recorded `RemoveRegimentFromUnit` (rva 0x1BE9A0); if it holds exactly one it takes a longer path through the game state, a localisation render and `ConcurrentQueue_MicroQueuePush` (0x28DA00), which is where disbanding the whole unit and telling the player would live. **That last path was not read.**
addresses.evidence: Decoded end to end from the entry; cfg.walk gives three `ret 8` and no `ret 0x28`, and slot 9 of the class is 0x5BC1E0, two bytes past the last ret. The receiver of slot 8 is the list node's payload (`mov eax,[edi]`). The compared string is `this` restored from the stack slot written at 0x5BBF37 before the three callee-save pushes, so its +0x20/+0x30/+0x34 are CStringEffect::text's data, length and capacity, which the already-recorded field names. `CUnit +0x38 regiments`, `+0x40 regiments_count` and `CSubUnit +0x68 name` were all already recorded. Shown wrong by: slot 8 of CRegiment returning something other than +0x68, or CSubUnit::SetType writing a type name into +0x68 - a decode of CSubUnit::SetType (rva 0x1ABF30) finds no write to +0x68, but that is a weaker check than reading a live regiment, so **what an unnamed regiment has in +0x68 is not established here**.

addresses.name: CCountryEventEffect::Execute
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CCountryEventEffect::Execute(CCountryEventEffect* this, CEventScope* scope, int unused)
addresses.comment: **`country_event`, 4,636 live instances.** 0x5AE3E0 to the one `ret 8` at 0x5AE51A, three int3 after. It builds a fresh 0x48-byte CEventScope on its stack rather than narrowing one: vftable 0x11B8AEC, token 0x18D, `random_state` and `seed` set to `(r1*r2) & 0x3FFFFFFF` from **two steps of the parent scope's own LCG, written back into the parent** (`scope->+8`), `country` copied from the parent's `country_tag`/`country_id`, and `from_country` taken from the parent's **`this_scope (+0x38)`** - or, when that scope has no country, its province copied into `from_province (+0x30)`. Then `eventId = this->+0x20 / 1000`, `FindPersistentById({0x28, eventId}, [0x1A857F4])`, and - this is the part a mod needs - **the target event's own `trigger` (+0x30) slot 6 is evaluated against the new scope and the event is only fired if it passes**, through the already-recorded `FireEvent` (0x5C0C80). A `country_event` pointing at an event whose trigger is false, or at an id that does not exist, is a silent no-op.
addresses.evidence: Decoded end to end. The /1000 is the 0x10624dd3 + `sar edx,6` idiom at 0x5AE4BA, which is the control on CIntEffect::TakeScalarValue's *1000. The scope's field offsets are the ones project.json already records for CEventScope, and the stack arithmetic was resolved against the `and esp,0xfffffff8; sub esp,0x54` frame plus three pushes. The trigger call is `[event->+0x30]->vftable[0x18]`, slot 6, which project.json records as CTrigger::Evaluate; project.json's comment on RunDailyEventPass already describes CEvent +0x30 as the event's trigger, reached the same way, although there is no CEvent struct field for it. Shown wrong by: the stack scope's base address being 4 or 8 bytes off, which would move every field attribution by the same amount - the vftable store at [esp+0x18] is the anchor.

addresses.name: CRandomEffect::Execute
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CRandomEffect::Execute(CRandomEffect* this, CEventScope* scope, int unused)
addresses.comment: **`random = { chance = N ... }`, and the whole of it is twenty instructions.** 0x5AF920 to the one `ret 8` at 0x5AF997, six int3 after. It runs **two** steps of MSVC's `rand` recurrence (0x343FD / 0x269EC3) on `scope->random_state (+0x8)` in place, takes the top 15 bits of each, multiplies them and takes the product modulo 100; if that is **strictly less than** `this->+0x20 / 1000` it runs the children, passing them a literal **0** as the second argument. So `chance` is a whole-number percentage, `chance = 100` always fires and `chance = 0` never does, the draw is deterministic given the scope's seed, and **evaluating a `random` block advances the scope's random state whether or not it fires**. The two-step recurrence and the state write-back are the same ones the `ally` and `local_enemy` contexts use through the LCG at rva 0x6A2E90, so an effect block's randomness and a trigger block's share one stream.
addresses.evidence: Decoded end to end; the recurrence constants, the `and eax,0x7fff` pair, `idiv 0x64` and the 0x10624dd3/sar 6 divide by 1000 are all in the twenty instructions, and `jge` past the loop makes the comparison strict. The state write-back is `mov [edi+8], eax` at 0x5AF943. Shown wrong by: +0x20 not holding the `chance` key, which CRandomEffect::LoadKey (already recorded, and its switch names exactly one key, `chance`) would settle.

addresses.name: CLoadOOBEffect::Execute
addresses.revises: the second stack argument is named rather than left as `unknown`, now that all 100 slot-11 bodies have been checked: nothing in the CEffect family reads it, two of them replace it with a literal 0, and the only two call sites found pass 0 and an event-option index. `unused` is what the executable supports; `unknown` overstated what is open.
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CLoadOOBEffect::Execute(CLoadOOBEffect* this, CEventScope* scope, int unused)
addresses.comment: Loads the order of battle the effect names: `CStringEffect::text` is written onto the country by CCountry::SetOobFile, and CCountry::LoadOobFile is called on it. The country is the scope's, by the id at `scope + 0x14`. **Nothing about the file is in memory before this**, which is why a tooltip about it has to read the file itself. The second stack argument is written out so the `ret 8` adds up and is read by nothing: of the 100 distinct slot-11 bodies in the CEffect family, 11 read it and all 11 only pass it on, while CRandomEffect and CContextEffect substitute a literal 0 - so no effect can see it. The name is BiceLib's.
addresses.evidence: The signature is unchanged in shape - still `ret 8` with two stack arguments - so the audit is unaffected; what changes is the parameter's name and the comment's claim about it. The scan behind that claim is over all 100 slot-11 bodies with extents bounded by the next known function entry, positive-controlled by the same scan finding [ebp+8] in 98 of them. Shown wrong by: a slot-11 body that consumes [ebp+0xC], or a caller whose behaviour depends on the value.

struct_fields.name: keyword
struct_fields.comment: **Which keyword built this effect.** Written in exactly one place, the common tail of CEffect::LoadKey at 0x59B630, from LoadKey's own `key` argument, and only when the switch actually made an object. Read by slot 6 (rva 0x16000, `mov eax,[ecx+0x18]; ret`), whose one caller is CEffect::GetBlockText - which uses it to group consecutive siblings built by the same keyword onto one comma-separated tooltip line. Not the same thing as CPersistent::token at +4.
struct_fields.evidence: A decode of all 8136 bytes of CEffect::LoadKey finds one non-esp write to +0x18, at 0x59B630, and cfg.py --lands-in shows every arm of the switch converges on 0x59B625 just above it. Shown wrong by: a writer outside CEffect::LoadKey, or slot 6 having another reader that means something else by it. This closes the '0x18 to 0x1F is not established' note in findings/FINDINGS-effecttext.md.

struct_fields.name: use_this
struct_fields.comment: **The value was the word `this`** (SaveToken 0x377) rather than a number or a tag, so the effect's target is the scope's own subject. Set by three unrelated slot-7 handlers at the same offset: CIntEffect's (0x59D4A0), CValueEffect's (0x59CB50) and, per findings/FINDINGS-script.md, the casus belli effects' - which is why the pair belongs to the common base rather than to any one of them.
struct_fields.evidence: `mov word ptr [ecx+0x1c], 0` then `cmp <token>, 0x377; mov byte ptr [ecx+0x1c], 1` in both 0x59CB50 and 0x59D4A0, and FINDINGS-script.md already describes +0x1C/+0x1D as the this/FROM flags on CCasusBelliEffect. Placing it on CEffect is **inference**: the three users are siblings, so their own data would start at the same offset either way. What settles it as the base's is that CFlagEffect's slot 7 puts its Hoi3CString at +0x20 and not at +0x1C, and every other subclass's own data starts at +0x20 too - so +0x18..+0x1F is base territory and CEffect is 0x20 bytes. Shown wrong by: a subclass that puts its own first field at +0x1C.

struct_fields.name: use_from
struct_fields.comment: **The value was the word `from`** (SaveToken 0x34F), so the effect's target is the scope's FROM. The other half of the pair at +0x1C, cleared with it as one word.
struct_fields.evidence: As +0x1C: `cmp <token>, 0x34f; mov byte ptr [ecx+0x1d], 1` in both scalar handlers, and the pair is cleared together with a single `mov word ptr [ecx+0x1c], 0`, which is how we know they are two bytes and not one dword. Shown wrong by the same thing as +0x1C.

struct_fields.name: national_unity
struct_fields.comment: **National unity, in thousandths, held between 1000 and 100000** - 1.0 to 100.0. Its only writer is CCountry::ChangeNationalUnity (rva 0xF8B80), which adds `delta * (1000 + global_modifier[MODIFIER_NATIONAL_UNITY_EFFECT]) / 1000` and then applies both clamps. It sits immediately after `dissent` at +0x10B4.
struct_fields.evidence: The clamps are the literals 0x186A0 and 0x3E8 in 0xF8B80, and the scaling modifier's index resolves to 0x44, which scripts/modifierIds.py names MODIFIER_NATIONAL_UNITY_EFFECT - the modifier's name is the independent evidence for the field's. Shown wrong by: another writer of CCountry +0x10B8. Note that CNavalCombatant also uses +0x10B8, for `positioning`; that is a different class and project.json's existing +0x10B8 comments are all about it.

struct_fields.name: neutrality
struct_fields.comment: **Neutrality**, written only by CCountry::ChangeNeutrality (rva 0xFBF80), floored at zero, with the derived EffectiveNeutrality at +0xA90. Named from the key CCountry::SaveContents writes it under.
struct_fields.evidence: Already named in BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp from the save key, and already described in project.json's comment on CCountry::ChangeNeutrality - but **not recorded as a field**, which is trap 14's two-halves problem. The reading here is a third, independent arrival: CNeutralityEffect::Execute (0x5B9740) calls that setter with the effect's own value. Shown wrong by: the save key pairing in CCountry::SaveContents being to a different offset.

struct_fields.name: flags
struct_fields.comment: **The global flags** - the tree `set_global_flag` and `clr_global_flag` write and `has_global_flag` reads, held by value. CGameState::CGameState writes CFlags' own vftable (0x15BB468, a virtual address) here and CFlags' CPersistent vftable at +0xE8, which is the +0x24 second base CFlags.hpp documents - so the field project.json has been calling `flags` at +0xE8 is that sub-object and the flags themselves start here. CSetGlobalFlagEffect::Execute dispatches slot 2 on this address.
struct_fields.evidence: `mov dword ptr [ebx+0xc4], 0x15bb468` at 0x27D155 and `mov dword ptr [ebx+0xe8], 0x15bb48c` at 0x27D15F, inside CGameState::CGameState (rva 0x27D070), 0x24 apart; and `lea esi,[eax+0xc4]` as the receiver in CSetGlobalFlagEffect::Execute. Shown wrong by: 0x15BB468 not being CFlags' primary vftable, which the RTTI export gives directly.

struct_fields.name: flags_persistent
struct_fields.revises: it is not the flags - it is the CPersistent second base of the CFlags that starts at +0xC4, 0x24 earlier, which is where the effects and the lookups actually go. The old record's own comment said 'saved as flags by calling slot 1 on the object here', which is exactly what a save routine does with a CPersistent sub-object, so the name was right about the save and wrong about the object.
struct_fields.comment: The CPersistent second base of `flags` (+0xC4), 0x24 into it, as CFlags.hpp describes. This is the sub-object CGameState::SaveContents calls slot 1 on to write the `flags` block, which is why it looked like the field. The tree itself is at +0xC4.
struct_fields.evidence: The two vftable stores in CGameState::CGameState, 0x24 apart, and CFlags.hpp's statement that CFlags has CPersistent as a second base at +0x24. Shown wrong by: a reader of +0xE8 that treats it as a CFlags rather than as a CPersistent - the three `set_*_flag` effects all take the CFlags address, not this one.

struct_fields.name: flags
struct_fields.comment: The global flags; CCurrentGameState derives from CGameState and adds nothing at this offset, so the field is the base's. See CGameState +0xC4.
struct_fields.evidence: As CGameState +0xC4; the record already carries the same duplication for +0xB8C and +0xBBC for the same reason. Shown wrong by the same thing.

struct_fields.name: flags_persistent
struct_fields.revises: the same correction as CGameState +0xE8: this is the CPersistent sub-object of the CFlags at +0xC4, not the flags.
struct_fields.comment: The CPersistent second base of `flags` (+0xC4). See CGameState +0xE8.
struct_fields.evidence: As CGameState +0xE8. Shown wrong by the same thing.

struct_fields.name: flags
struct_fields.comment: **The province's flags** - what `set_province_flag`, `clr_province_flag` and `has_province_flag` work on, held by value. CProvince::CProvince writes CFlags' vftable here and its CPersistent vftable at +0xC4, 0x24 later; the field project.json has been calling `flags` at +0xC4 is that sub-object.
struct_fields.evidence: `mov dword ptr [esi+0xa0], 0x15bb468` at 0x494807 and `mov dword ptr [esi+0xc4], 0x15bb48c` at 0x494811, inside the constructor at rva 0x94700 which writes CProvince's own two vftables (0x15BEB80 and 0x15BEBA4) at 0x49473B and 0x494741; and `[esi+0xa0]` as the receiver in CSetProvinceFlagEffect::Execute. Shown wrong by: that constructor belonging to another class, or the effect reaching the tree some other way.

struct_fields.name: flags_persistent
struct_fields.revises: it is the CPersistent second base of the CFlags that starts at +0xA0, not the flags. BiceLib/GameClasses/CMapProvince.hpp already calls it 'a CPersistent of its own', which is right; what was wrong was the name, since reading a flag tree from here through CTernary::Offsets::root would read +0xC8 and the root is at +0xA4.
struct_fields.comment: The CPersistent second base of `flags` (+0xA0), 0x24 into it. This is the sub-object the save calls slot 1 on to write the province's `flags` block. The tree itself is at +0xA0.
struct_fields.evidence: The two vftable stores in CProvince::CProvince, 0x24 apart, against CFlags.hpp's +0x24 second base. Shown wrong by: a reader of +0xC4 that treats it as a CFlags.

struct_fields.name: flags
struct_fields.comment: The province's flags, held by value; CMapProvince derives from CProvince, whose constructor places it. See CProvince +0xA0.
struct_fields.evidence: As CProvince +0xA0. Shown wrong by the same thing.

struct_fields.name: flags_persistent
struct_fields.revises: the same correction as CProvince +0xC4: this is the CPersistent sub-object of the CFlags at +0xA0.
struct_fields.comment: The CPersistent second base of `flags` (+0xA0). See CProvince +0xC4.
struct_fields.evidence: As CProvince +0xC4. Shown wrong by the same thing.
